    "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/ibm-plex/IBMPlexSans-Regular.ttf",
    "/usr/share/fonts/opentype/ibm-plex/IBMPlexSans-Regular.otf",
    "/usr/share/fonts/windows/ZedMonoNerdFont-Regular.ttf",
];

#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
const KNOWN_UI_PATHS: &[&str] = &[];

/// Well-known Monospace font paths (Zed Mono / IBM Plex Mono).
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
const KNOWN_MONO_PATHS: &[&str] = &[
    "/usr/share/fonts/windows/ZedMonoNerdFontMono-Regular.ttf",
    "/usr/share/fonts/windows/ZedMonoNerdFont-Regular.ttf",
    "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/ibm-plex/IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf",
    "/usr/share/fonts/opentype/ibm-plex/IBMPlexMono-Regular.otf",
];

#[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
const KNOWN_MONO_PATHS: &[&str] = &[];

/// UI font family preference list.
const PREFERRED_UI_FAMILIES: &[&str] = &[
    "IBM Plex Sans",
    "ZedMono Nerd Font Propo",
    "ZedMono NFP",
    "ZedMono Nerd Font",
    "Inter",
    "Cantarell",
    "Noto Sans",
    "Segoe UI",
];

/// Monospace font family preference list.
const PREFERRED_MONO_FAMILIES: &[&str] = &[
    "ZedMono Nerd Font Mono",
    "ZedMono NFM",
    "ZedMono Nerd Font",
    "IBM Plex Mono",
    "JetBrains Mono",
    "DejaVu Sans Mono",
];

/// Try to find a Zed-like UI font.
pub fn find_ui_font() -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    for path in KNOWN_UI_PATHS {
        if let Ok(data) = std::fs::read(path) {
            if !data.is_empty() {
                return Some(LoadedFont {
                    family: file_stem(path),
                    data,
                    index: 0,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    scan_families(PREFERRED_UI_FAMILIES)
}

/// Try to find a Zed-like Monospace font.
pub fn find_mono_font() -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    for path in KNOWN_MONO_PATHS {
        if let Ok(data) = std::fs::read(path) {
            if !data.is_empty() {
                return Some(LoadedFont {
                    family: file_stem(path),
                    data,
                    index: 0,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    scan_families(PREFERRED_MONO_FAMILIES)
}

/// Family name of the UI font installed at startup.
static INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY: std::sync::OnceLock<Option<String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Family name of the UI font in use.
pub fn installed_ui_family() -> Option<String> {
    INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.get().cloned().flatten()
}

/// Try to find a CJK-capable system font.
pub fn find_cjk_font() -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    for path in KNOWN_PATHS {
        if let Ok(data) = std::fs::read(path) {
            if !data.is_empty() {
                return Some(LoadedFont {
                    family: file_stem(path),
                    data,
                    index: 0,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    scan_families(PREFERRED_FAMILIES)
}

/// Ask `fontdb` for an installed family from `preferred`.
fn scan_families(preferred: &[&str]) -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    let mut db = fontdb::Database::new();
    db.load_system_fonts();

    for wanted in preferred {
        let family = db
            .faces()
            .find(|face| {
                face.families
                    .iter()
                    .any(|(name, _)| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(wanted))
            })
            .map(|face| {
                (
                    face.id,
                    face.index,
                    face.families.first().map(|(n, _)| n.clone()),
                )
            });
        let Some((id, index, name)) = family else {
            continue;
        };
        let data = db.with_face_data(id, |bytes, _| bytes.to_vec())?;
        if data.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        return Some(LoadedFont {
            family: name.unwrap_or_else(|| (*wanted).to_owned()),
            data,
            index,
        });
    }
    None
}

/// Extract the file name without its extension.
///
/// Both separators are handled explicitly rather than deferring to
/// `Path::file_stem`, so the Windows path list produces sensible names even
/// when this code is compiled and tested on Unix.
fn file_stem(path: &str) -> String {
    let name = path.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or(path);
    match name.rsplit_once('.') {
        Some((stem, _)) if !stem.is_empty() => stem.to_owned(),
        _ => name.to_owned(),
    }
}

/// The result of installing fonts into an egui context.
pub enum FontStatus {
    /// A CJK font was installed.
    Loaded(String),
    /// No CJK font was found; Chinese text will not render.
    Missing,
}

/// Family name of the font installed at startup.
///
/// Cached rather than re-discovered: the lookup reads a multi-megabyte font
/// file, so it must happen exactly once.
static INSTALLED_FAMILY: std::sync::OnceLock<Option<String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Family name of the CJK font in use, or `None` when none was found.
pub fn installed_family() -> Option<String> {
    INSTALLED_FAMILY.get().cloned().flatten()
}

/// Install the application font stack.
///
/// Zed default UI font is made primary for proportional text, Zed Mono for
/// monospace text, and the CJK face is appended as fallback for both.
pub fn install(ctx: &egui::Context) -> FontStatus {
    let mut fonts = egui::FontDefinitions::default();

    if let Some(ui_font) = find_ui_font() {
        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(ui_font.data);
        data.index = ui_font.index;
        fonts.font_data.insert("zed_ui".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));
        fonts
            .families
            .entry(egui::FontFamily::Proportional)
            .or_default()
            .insert(0, "zed_ui".to_owned());
        let _ = INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.set(Some(ui_font.family));
    } else {
        let _ = INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.set(None);
    }

    if let Some(mono_font) = find_mono_font() {
        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(mono_font.data);
        data.index = mono_font.index;
        fonts.font_data.insert("zed_mono".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));
        fonts
            .families
            .entry(egui::FontFamily::Monospace)
            .or_default()
            .insert(0, "zed_mono".to_owned());
    }

    let cjk = find_cjk_font();
    if let Some(ref font) = cjk {
        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(font.data.clone());
        data.index = font.index;
        fonts.font_data.insert("cjk".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));

        for family in [egui::FontFamily::Proportional, egui::FontFamily::Monospace] {
            fonts
                .families
                .entry(family)
                .or_default()
                .push("cjk".to_owned());
        }
    }

    ctx.set_fonts(fonts);

    match cjk {
        Some(font) => {
            let _ = INSTALLED_FAMILY.set(Some(font.family.clone()));
            FontStatus::Loaded(font.family)
        }
        None => {
            let _ = INSTALLED_FAMILY.set(None);
            FontStatus::Missing
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn preferred_families_are_non_empty_and_unique() {
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for name in PREFERRED_FAMILIES {
            assert!(!name.is_empty());
            assert!(seen.insert(*name), "duplicate family {name}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_stem_strips_directory_and_extension() {
        assert_eq!(
            file_stem("/usr/share/fonts/x/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc"),
            "NotoSansCJK-Regular"
        );
        assert_eq!(file_stem("C:\\Windows\\Fonts\\msyh.ttc"), "msyh");
    }

    #[test]
    fn zed_font_can_be_found() {
        if let Some(font) = find_ui_font() {
            assert!(!font.data.is_empty());
            assert!(!font.family.is_empty());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn detection_never_panics() {
        // The result depends on the host, so only assert it is well formed.
        if let Some(font) = find_cjk_font() {
            assert!(!font.data.is_empty());
            assert!(!font.family.is_empty());
        }
    }
}

-- theme --
//! Dark and light themes, and the colours used by the receive log.
//!
//! The original tool ships a black-background/green-text terminal look, plus a
//! "白底黑字" (white background, black text) alternative.  Both are preserved
//! here as the *log* palettes of the two themes, while the surrounding
//! application chrome follows a conventional dark/light widget theme.

use eframe::egui::{self, Color32, Stroke, Visuals};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Which theme the application should use.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ThemeMode {
    /// Classic terminal look: black log, green text.
    #[default]
    Dark,
    /// 白底黑字: white log, black text.
    Light,
    /// Follow the operating system preference.
    System,
}

impl ThemeMode {
    pub const ALL: [ThemeMode; 3] = [ThemeMode::Dark, ThemeMode::Light, ThemeMode::System];

    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ThemeMode::Dark => "黑色主题",
            ThemeMode::Light => "白色主题",
            ThemeMode::System => "跟随系统",
        }
    }

    pub fn icon(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ThemeMode::Dark => "🌙",
            ThemeMode::Light => "☀",
            ThemeMode::System => "🖥",
        }
    }
}

/// Colours for the receive log area.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LogPalette {
    pub background: Color32,
    pub foreground: Color32,
    /// Colour of the `[HH:MM:SS.mmm]` prefix.
    pub timestamp: Color32,
    /// Selection highlight.
    pub selection: Color32,
    /// Text of the selection.
    pub selection_text: Color32,
    /// Rows echoed back from our own transmissions.
    pub sent: Color32,
}

/// The classic XCOM terminal look.
pub const DARK_LOG: LogPalette = LogPalette {
    background: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0x00, 0x00),
    foreground: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0xFF, 0x00),
    timestamp: Color32::from_rgb(0x6A, 0xA8, 0x6A),
    selection: Color32::from_rgb(0x1E, 0x4D, 0x2E),
    selection_text: Color32::from_rgb(0xEA, 0xFF, 0xEA),
    // Amber reads clearly against the green of received data.
    sent: Color32::from_rgb(0xFF, 0xB7, 0x4D),
};

/// 白底黑字.
pub const LIGHT_LOG: LogPalette = LogPalette {
    background: Color32::from_rgb(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF),
    foreground: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0x00, 0x00),
    timestamp: Color32::from_rgb(0x80, 0x80, 0x80),
    selection: Color32::from_rgb(0xCC, 0xE4, 0xFF),
    selection_text: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0x00, 0x00),
    sent: Color32::from_rgb(0xB2, 0x5E, 0x00),
};

/// User override for the log colours.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct LogColorOverride {
    /// When false the theme's default log palette is used.
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub foreground: [u8; 3],
    pub background: [u8; 3],
}

impl Default for LogColorOverride {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            enabled: false,
            foreground: [0x00, 0xFF, 0x00],
            background: [0x00, 0x00, 0x00],
        }
    }
}

impl LogColorOverride {
    /// Apply the override on top of a theme palette.
    pub fn apply(self, base: LogPalette) -> LogPalette {
        if !self.enabled {
            return base;
        }
        let foreground =
            Color32::from_rgb(self.foreground[0], self.foreground[1], self.foreground[2]);
        let background =
            Color32::from_rgb(self.background[0], self.background[1], self.background[2]);
        // Keep the selection legible against whatever background was chosen.
        let selection = blend(background, foreground, 0.35);
        LogPalette {
            background,
            foreground,
            selection,
            selection_text: foreground,
            // Timestamps stay distinguishable without clashing.
            timestamp: blend(background, foreground, 0.65),
            // A custom foreground/background pair says nothing about which hue
            // suits echoed rows, so the theme's choice is kept.
            sent: base.sent,
        }
    }
}

/// Linear blend between two colours; `t` of 0 yields `a`, 1 yields `b`.
fn blend(a: Color32, b: Color32, t: f32) -> Color32 {
    let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
    let mix = |x: u8, y: u8| (x as f32 + (y as f32 - x as f32) * t).round() as u8;
    Color32::from_rgb(mix(a.r(), b.r()), mix(a.g(), b.g()), mix(a.b(), b.b()))
}

/// Background colour of the application chrome (panels and status bar).
///
/// Also used as the window backdrop, which is why it is public: the rounded
/// window background is painted in this colour.
pub fn panel_background(dark: bool) -> Color32 {
    if dark {
        Color32::from_rgb(0x1E, 0x1E, 0x1E)
    } else {
        Color32::from_rgb(0xF3, 0xF3, 0xF3)
    }
}

/// Whether the given mode currently resolves to a dark appearance.
pub fn is_dark(ctx: &egui::Context, mode: ThemeMode) -> bool {
    match mode {
        ThemeMode::Dark => true,
        ThemeMode::Light => false,
        ThemeMode::System => ctx.theme() == egui::Theme::Dark,
    }
}

/// The log palette in effect.
pub fn log_palette(ctx: &egui::Context, mode: ThemeMode, over: LogColorOverride) -> LogPalette {
    let base = if is_dark(ctx, mode) {
        DARK_LOG
    } else {
        LIGHT_LOG
    };
    over.apply(base)
}

/// Install the widget visuals for both themes and select the active one.
///
/// Called only when the mode changes, not every frame.
pub fn apply(ctx: &egui::Context, mode: ThemeMode) {
    ctx.set_visuals_of(egui::Theme::Dark, tuned_dark());
    ctx.set_visuals_of(egui::Theme::Light, tuned_light());
    ctx.set_theme(match mode {
        ThemeMode::Dark => egui::ThemePreference::Dark,
        ThemeMode::Light => egui::ThemePreference::Light,
        ThemeMode::System => egui::ThemePreference::System,
    });
    ctx.all_styles_mut(|style| {
        style.spacing.item_spacing = egui::vec2(8.0, 6.0);
        style.spacing.button_padding = egui::vec2(8.0, 4.0);
    });
}

/// A slightly calmer dark theme than egui's default, closer to a native tool.
fn tuned_dark() -> Visuals {
    let mut v = Visuals::dark();
    let panel = Color32::from_rgb(0x1E, 0x1E, 0x1E);
    let surface = Color32::from_rgb(0x25, 0x25, 0x26);
    let field = Color32::from_rgb(0x14, 0x14, 0x14);
    let accent = Color32::from_rgb(0x2E, 0x86, 0xDE);

    // When the application paints its own rounded window background, the
    // panels must not paint square corners over it.
    v.panel_fill = if crate::ui::window::PAINTS_OWN_BACKGROUND {
        Color32::TRANSPARENT
    } else {
        panel
    };
    v.window_fill = surface;
    v.extreme_bg_color = field;
    v.faint_bg_color = Color32::from_rgb(0x2A, 0x2A, 0x2B);
    v.code_bg_color = field;
    v.selection.bg_fill = accent.gamma_multiply(0.45);
    v.selection.stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, Color32::from_rgb(0xC8, 0xDC, 0xF0));
    v.hyperlink_color = Color32::from_rgb(0x54, 0xA6, 0xF0);
    v.window_stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, Color32::from_rgb(0x3A, 0x3A, 0x3C));
    v.widgets.noninteractive.bg_fill = panel;
    v.widgets.inactive.bg_fill = Color32::from_rgb(0x33, 0x33, 0x35);
    v.widgets.hovered.bg_fill = Color32::from_rgb(0x3E, 0x3E, 0x41);
    v.widgets.active.bg_fill = accent.gamma_multiply(0.7);

    v.widgets.noninteractive.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v.widgets.inactive.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v.widgets.hovered.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v.widgets.active.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v
}

/// A light theme with neutral greys rather than egui's blue-tinted default.
fn tuned_light() -> Visuals {
    let mut v = Visuals::light();
    let panel = Color32::from_rgb(0xF3, 0xF3, 0xF3);
    let surface = Color32::from_rgb(0xFA, 0xFA, 0xFA);
    let field = Color32::from_rgb(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF);
    let accent = Color32::from_rgb(0x2E, 0x86, 0xDE);

    v.panel_fill = if crate::ui::window::PAINTS_OWN_BACKGROUND {
        Color32::TRANSPARENT
    } else {
        panel
    };
    v.window_fill = surface;
    v.extreme_bg_color = field;
    v.faint_bg_color = Color32::from_rgb(0xE9, 0xE9, 0xEA);
    v.code_bg_color = field;
    v.selection.bg_fill = accent.gamma_multiply(0.35);
    v.selection.stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, Color32::from_rgb(0x20, 0x40, 0x60));
    v.hyperlink_color = Color32::from_rgb(0x1B, 0x62, 0xB0);
    v.window_stroke = Stroke::new(1.0, Color32::from_rgb(0xD0, 0xD0, 0xD2));
    v.widgets.noninteractive.bg_fill = panel;
    v.widgets.inactive.bg_fill = Color32::from_rgb(0xE0, 0xE0, 0xE2);
    v.widgets.hovered.bg_fill = Color32::from_rgb(0xD5, 0xD5, 0xD8);
    v.widgets.active.bg_fill = accent.gamma_multiply(0.6);

    v.widgets.noninteractive.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v.widgets.inactive.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v.widgets.hovered.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v.widgets.active.corner_radius = egui::CornerRadius::same(4);
    v
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn dark_log_is_the_classic_terminal_look() {
        assert_eq!(DARK_LOG.background, Color32::BLACK);
        assert_eq!(DARK_LOG.foreground.g(), 0xFF, "green text");
        assert_eq!(DARK_LOG.foreground.r(), 0x00);
    }

    #[test]
    fn light_log_is_white_on_black() {
        assert_eq!(LIGHT_LOG.background, Color32::WHITE);
        assert_eq!(LIGHT_LOG.foreground, Color32::BLACK);
    }

    #[test]
    fn disabled_override_passes_the_theme_through() {
        let over = LogColorOverride::default();
        assert_eq!(over.apply(DARK_LOG), DARK_LOG);
        assert_eq!(over.apply(LIGHT_LOG), LIGHT_LOG);
    }

    #[test]
    fn enabled_override_replaces_both_colours() {
        let over = LogColorOverride {
            enabled: true,
            foreground: [0x11, 0x22, 0x33],
            background: [0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC],
        };
        let palette = over.apply(DARK_LOG);
        assert_eq!(palette.foreground, Color32::from_rgb(0x11, 0x22, 0x33));
        assert_eq!(palette.background, Color32::from_rgb(0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC));
        // Derived colours must be plausible and not equal to either input.
        assert_ne!(palette.selection, palette.background);
        assert_ne!(palette.timestamp, palette.background);
    }

    #[test]
    fn blend_endpoints_are_exact() {
        let a = Color32::from_rgb(0, 0, 0);
        let b = Color32::from_rgb(255, 128, 64);
        assert_eq!(blend(a, b, 0.0), a);
        assert_eq!(blend(a, b, 1.0), b);
        assert_eq!(blend(a, b, 0.5), Color32::from_rgb(128, 64, 32));
        // Out-of-range t is clamped rather than wrapping.
        assert_eq!(blend(a, b, -1.0), a);
        assert_eq!(blend(a, b, 2.0), b);
    }

    #[test]
    fn theme_mode_labels_are_distinct() {
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for mode in ThemeMode::ALL {
            assert!(seen.insert(mode.label()));
            assert!(!mode.icon().is_empty());
        }
    }
}

/// How the view should behave this frame.
pub struct LogViewOptions {
    pub auto_scroll: bool,
    pub font_size: f32,
    pub line_spacing: f32,
}

/// Actions the surrounding UI should perform, requested from the view.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct LogViewOutput {
    /// The selection was copied to the clipboard by the view itself.
    pub copied: bool,
    /// A selection exists and could be copied.
    pub has_selection: bool,
}

/// Everything needed to hit-test and paint one visible row.
struct VisibleRow {
    index: usize,
    /// Stable id, used by carets so they survive trimming.
    row_id: u64,
    galley: Arc<Galley>,
    origin: Pos2,
    rect: Rect,
    /// Colour this row is drawn in, which the galley bakes in.
    color: Color32,
}

/// Draw the log and handle interaction.
pub fn show(
    ui: &mut Ui,
    store: &LogStore,
    palette: LogPalette,
    state: &mut LogViewState,
    options: &LogViewOptions,
) -> LogViewOutput {
    let font = FontId::monospace(options.font_size);
    let row_height = ui.ctx().fonts_mut(|f| f.row_height(&font)) + options.line_spacing;
    let char_width = ui.ctx().fonts_mut(|f| f.glyph_width(&font, 'M'));
    let total_rows = store.row_count();

    let mut output = LogViewOutput::default();

    if total_rows == 0 {
        // Still draw the (empty) background so the theme colour shows through.
        let (rect, response) =
            ui.allocate_exact_size(ui.available_size_before_wrap(), Sense::click_and_drag());
        ui.painter()
            .rect_filled(rect, egui::CornerRadius::ZERO, palette.background);
        let _ = response;
        return output;
    }

    let scroll = ScrollArea::both()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .stick_to_bottom(options.auto_scroll && !state.has_selection());

    let clip_rect = ui.clip_rect();
    let result = scroll.show(ui, |ui| {
        let content_width =
            (store.max_columns() as f32 * char_width + 12.0).max(ui.available_width());
        let content_height = total_rows as f32 * row_height;
        let (rect, response) = ui.allocate_exact_size(
            Vec2::new(content_width, content_height),
            Sense::click_and_drag(),
        );

        // Only these rows are laid out this frame.
        let viewport = clip_rect.intersect(rect);
        let first = if viewport.height() <= 0.0 {
            0
        } else {
            (((viewport.top() - rect.top()) / row_height)
                .floor()
                .max(0.0) as usize)
                .min(total_rows)
        };
        let last = if viewport.height() <= 0.0 {
            0
        } else {
            ((((viewport.bottom() - rect.top()) / row_height).ceil() as usize) + 1).min(total_rows)
        };

        let mut visible: Vec<VisibleRow> = Vec::with_capacity(last.saturating_sub(first));
        for index in first..last {
            let text = store.row(index).to_owned();
            // Echoed transmissions are tinted so they are not mistaken for
            // data from the device.
            let color = match store.row_kind(index) {
                RowKind::Received => palette.foreground,
                RowKind::Sent => palette.sent,
            };
            let galley = ui
                .ctx()
                .fonts_mut(|f| f.layout_no_wrap(text, font.clone(), color));
            let origin = Pos2::new(rect.left(), rect.top() + index as f32 * row_height);
            let row_rect = Rect::from_min_size(
                origin,
                Vec2::new(content_width.max(rect.width()), row_height),
            );
            visible.push(VisibleRow {
                index,
                row_id: store.row_id(index),
                galley,
                origin,
                rect: row_rect,
                color,
            });
        }

        // ---- interaction (before painting so the highlight is current) ----
        let pointer = response.interact_pointer_pos();
        if response.drag_started() {
            if let Some(pos) = pointer {
                if let Some(caret) = hit_test(&visible, rect, row_height, pos) {
                    state.drag_anchor = Some(caret);
                    state.selection = Some(Selection {
                        anchor: caret,
                        head: caret,
                    });
                }
            }
        } else if response.dragged() {
            if let (Some(pos), Some(anchor)) = (pointer, state.drag_anchor) {
                if let Some(caret) = hit_test_clamped(&visible, rect, row_height, pos) {
                    state.selection = Some(Selection {
                        anchor,
                        head: caret,
                    });

-- app draw --
    fn clear_color(&self, visuals: &egui::Visuals) -> [f32; 4] {
        crate::ui::window::clear_color(crate::theme::panel_background(visuals.dark_mode))
    }

    fn on_exit(&mut self, _gl: Option<&eframe::glow::Context>) {
        self.settings.window_size = None;
        if let Err(err) = self.settings.save() {
            log::error!("退出时保存设置失败: {err}");
        }
    }
}

impl XcomApp {
    /// Draw one complete frame.
    ///
    /// eframe 0.36 roots the app at a `Ui` rather than a `Context`, so the
    /// context is taken from it and used for the top-level panels.  Split out
    /// of the `App` impl so the headless test can lay out a real frame.
    pub(crate) fn draw(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) {
        let ctx = ui.ctx().clone();
        let ctx = &ctx;

        // The window backdrop goes down first, so every panel paints on top of
        // it.  Panels are transparent on platforms where we own the frame (see
        // `ui::window`), otherwise they would square off the bottom corners.
        crate::ui::window::paint_background(
            ui,
            crate::theme::panel_background(crate::theme::is_dark(ctx, self.settings.theme)),
        );

        // Styling only needs to be re-applied when the theme changes.
        let theme = self.settings.theme;
        if self.applied_theme != Some(theme) {
            crate::theme::apply(ctx, theme);
            self.applied_theme = Some(theme);
        }
        // The title bar is not re-read from the app, so switching language has
        // to push a new one; otherwise a Chinese UI keeps an English title
        // until the next launch.
        let language = crate::i18n::lang();
        if self.applied_lang != Some(language) {
            self.applied_lang = Some(language);
            ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Title(crate::i18n::window_title()));
        }

        // egui's default grab band is 5 px, which is easy to miss and presents
        // as "the separator cannot be dragged at all".
        ui.style_mut().interaction.resize_grab_radius_side = 8.0;

        self.note_font_status();

        self.pump_serial(ctx);
        self.pump_timers(ctx);
        self.handle_shortcuts(ctx);

        panels::top_bar(self, ui);
        panels::status_bar(self, ui);
        panels::left_panel(self, ui);
        if self.show_side_panel {
            panels::side_panel(self, ui);
        }
        panels::center_panel(self, ui);
        panels::apply_splitters(self, ui);
        panels::about_window(self, ctx);

        self.maybe_save_settings(ctx);
    }
}

/// Draw the receive log.  Kept here so the panel code can call it without
/// depending on the log view module's internals.
pub(crate) fn draw_log(
    app: &mut XcomApp,
    ui: &mut egui::Ui,
    palette: crate::theme::LogPalette,
) -> log_view::LogViewOutput {
    let options = LogViewOptions {
        auto_scroll: app.settings.auto_scroll,
        font_size: app.settings.log_font_size,
        line_spacing: app.settings.line_spacing,
    };

    // Tell the store how many columns fit, so text wrapping matches the panel.
    let font = egui::FontId::monospace(app.settings.log_font_size);
    let char_width = ui.ctx().fonts_mut(|f| f.glyph_width(&font, 'M'));
    if char_width > 0.0 && app.settings.display.wrap {
        let cols = (ui.available_width() / char_width).floor().max(8.0) as usize;
        app.update_wrap_width(cols, ui.ctx());
    }
    // `show` needs &LogStore and &mut LogViewState from the same struct.
    let XcomApp { log, log_view, .. } = app;
    log_view::show(ui, log, palette, log_view, &options)
}

-- README config --
```bash
cargo build --release
./packaging/install-user.sh          # 卸载：--uninstall
```

安装脚本会先做一次**启动耗时自检**（实测约 130 ms），再安装到 Debian 期望的
用户级位置，并在最后**检查 `TryExec` 是否能解析到命令**：

```
~/.local/bin/xcom                                  # 在 PATH 上，所以 Exec=xcom 可用
~/.local/share/applications/xcom.desktop
~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/<size>x<size>/apps/xcom.png   # 48/64/128/256/512
```

**`StartupNotify` 必须为 `false`（模板已如此）。** 它表示"应用会在启动完成后
发出握手信号"（`_NET_STARTUP_INFO` / activation token）。winit 把这个握手机制
做成**需要应用主动调用的 API**，而 egui/eframe 从不调用它。若声明为 `true`，
Dock 会一直停留在"正在启动"状态直到该承诺超时 —— 表现为**窗口早已出现，
但任务栏要等好几秒才显示正确图标**。声明 `false` 后，窗口可通过 app id 立即匹配。

**`TryExec` 是最容易踩的坑**：它在 **PATH** 上解析，而不是相对 `Exec`。
把 `Exec` 写成绝对路径、却把 `TryExec` 留成裸名字，会导致 `TryExec` 找不到命令，
而 **GNOME 会直接忽略整个条目** —— 菜单里没有图标也没有项，即使图标文件都在。
模板里这一行**默认注释掉**。

图标由 `packaging/make-icons.py` 按各尺寸分别绘制（而不是缩放同一张位图），
以保证 48px 下依然清晰：

```bash
python3 packaging/make-icons.py
```

`packaging/xcom.desktop` 是一份**逐键注释的模板**，可直接改用：

- 修改后用 Debian 自带的校验器确认，**它必须没有任何输出**：
  ```bash
  desktop-file-validate packaging/xcom.desktop
  ```
- `Categories` 只能有**一个主分类**。本项目用 `Development;Electronics;`——
  主分类 `Development` 加附加分类 `Electronics`。之前写的
  `Development;Electronics;Utility;` 含两个主分类，会让应用在菜单里出现两次，
  校验器会给出提示。
- `Icon` 只能是**图标名**，不能带路径或扩展名；图标通过 hicolor 主题解析。
- 所有列表型键（`Categories`、`Keywords`）必须以 `;` 结尾。
- `StartupWMClass` 在 Wayland 下必须等于应用 id，即
  `src/main.rs` 里的 `with_app_id("xcom")`；X11 下等于窗口的 `WM_CLASS`。

## 配置文件

设置保存在：

| 平台 | 路径 |
| --- | --- |
| Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/xcom/settings.json` 或 `~/.config/xcom/settings.json` |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\xcom\settings.json` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/xcom/settings.json` |

文件为可读的 JSON，可以直接编辑。字段使用 `#[serde(default)]`，**旧版本写入的配置在
新版本中仍可加载**（缺失字段取默认值）。写入采用「临时文件 + 重命名」，中断不会留下半个文件；
配置损坏时会回退到默认值而不是启动失败。

/// Try to find a CJK-capable system font.
pub fn find_cjk_font() -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    for path in KNOWN_PATHS {
        if let Ok(data) = std::fs::read(path) {
            if !data.is_empty() {
                return Some(LoadedFont {
                    family: file_stem(path),
                    data,
                    index: 0,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    scan_families(PREFERRED_FAMILIES)
}

/// Ask `fontdb` for an installed family from `preferred`.
fn scan_families(preferred: &[&str]) -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    let mut db = fontdb::Database::new();
    db.load_system_fonts();

    for wanted in preferred {
        let family = db
            .faces()
            .find(|face| {
                face.families
                    .iter()
                    .any(|(name, _)| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(wanted))
            })
            .map(|face| {
                (
                    face.id,
                    face.index,
                    face.families.first().map(|(n, _)| n.clone()),
                )
            });
        let Some((id, index, name)) = family else {
            continue;
        };
        let data = db.with_face_data(id, |bytes, _| bytes.to_vec())?;
        if data.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        return Some(LoadedFont {
            family: name.unwrap_or_else(|| (*wanted).to_owned()),
            data,
            index,
        });
    }
    None
}

/// Extract the file name without its extension.
///
/// Both separators are handled explicitly rather than deferring to
/// `Path::file_stem`, so the Windows path list produces sensible names even
/// when this code is compiled and tested on Unix.
fn file_stem(path: &str) -> String {
    let name = path.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or(path);
    match name.rsplit_once('.') {
        Some((stem, _)) if !stem.is_empty() => stem.to_owned(),
        _ => name.to_owned(),
    }
}

/// The result of installing fonts into an egui context.
pub enum FontStatus {
    /// A CJK font was installed.
    Loaded(String),
    /// No CJK font was found; Chinese text will not render.
    Missing,
}

/// Family name of the font installed at startup.
///
/// Cached rather than re-discovered: the lookup reads a multi-megabyte font
/// file, so it must happen exactly once.
static INSTALLED_FAMILY: std::sync::OnceLock<Option<String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Family name of the CJK font in use, or `None` when none was found.
pub fn installed_family() -> Option<String> {
    INSTALLED_FAMILY.get().cloned().flatten()
}

/// Install the application font stack.
///
/// Zed default UI font is made primary for proportional text, Zed Mono for
/// monospace text, and the CJK face is appended as fallback for both.
pub fn install(ctx: &egui::Context) -> FontStatus {
    let mut fonts = egui::FontDefinitions::default();

    if let Some(ui_font) = find_ui_font() {
        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(ui_font.data);
        data.index = ui_font.index;
        fonts.font_data.insert("zed_ui".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));
        fonts
            .families
            .entry(egui::FontFamily::Proportional)
            .or_default()
            .insert(0, "zed_ui".to_owned());
        let _ = INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.set(Some(ui_font.family));
    } else {
        let _ = INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.set(None);
    }

    if let Some(mono_font) = find_mono_font() {
        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(mono_font.data);
        data.index = mono_font.index;
        fonts.font_data.insert("zed_mono".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));
        fonts
            .families
            .entry(egui::FontFamily::Monospace)
            .or_default()
            .insert(0, "zed_mono".to_owned());
    }

    let cjk = find_cjk_font();
    if let Some(ref font) = cjk {
        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(font.data.clone());
        data.index = font.index;
        fonts.font_data.insert("cjk".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));

        for family in [egui::FontFamily::Proportional, egui::FontFamily::Monospace] {
            fonts
                .families
                .entry(family)
                .or_default()
                .push("cjk".to_owned());
        }
    }

    ctx.set_fonts(fonts);

    match cjk {
        Some(font) => {
            let _ = INSTALLED_FAMILY.set(Some(font.family.clone()));
            FontStatus::Loaded(font.family)
        }
        None => {
            let _ = INSTALLED_FAMILY.set(None);
            FontStatus::Missing
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn preferred_families_are_non_empty_and_unique() {
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for name in PREFERRED_FAMILIES {
            assert!(!name.is_empty());
            assert!(seen.insert(*name), "duplicate family {name}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn file_stem_strips_directory_and_extension() {
        assert_eq!(
            file_stem("/usr/share/fonts/x/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc"),
            "NotoSansCJK-Regular"
        );
        assert_eq!(file_stem("C:\\Windows\\Fonts\\msyh.ttc"), "msyh");
    }

    #[test]
    fn zed_font_can_be_found() {
        if let Some(font) = find_ui_font() {
            assert!(!font.data.is_empty());
            assert!(!font.family.is_empty());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn detection_never_panics() {
        // The result depends on the host, so only assert it is well formed.
        if let Some(font) = find_cjk_font() {
            assert!(!font.data.is_empty());
            assert!(!font.family.is_empty());
        }
    }
}

   125	/// Linear blend between two colours; `t` of 0 yields `a`, 1 yields `b`.
   126	fn blend(a: Color32, b: Color32, t: f32) -> Color32 {

   128	    let mix = |x: u8, y: u8| (x as f32 + (y as f32 - x as f32) * t).round() as u8;
   129	    Color32::from_rgb(mix(a.r(), b.r()), mix(a.g(), b.g()), mix(a.b(), b.b()))

/// Family name of the UI font installed at startup.
static INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY: std::sync::OnceLock<Option<String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Family name of the UI font in use.
pub fn installed_ui_family() -> Option<String> {
    INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.get().cloned().flatten()
}

/// Try to find a CJK-capable system font.
pub fn find_cjk_font() -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    for path in KNOWN_PATHS {
        if let Ok(data) = std::fs::read(path) {
            if !data.is_empty() {
                return Some(LoadedFont {
                    family: file_stem(path),
                    data,
                    index: 0,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    scan_families(PREFERRED_FAMILIES)
}

/// Ask `fontdb` for an installed family from `preferred`.
fn scan_families(preferred: &[&str]) -> Option<LoadedFont> {
    let mut db = fontdb::Database::new();
    db.load_system_fonts();

    for wanted in preferred {
        let family = db
            .faces()
            .find(|face| {
                face.families
                    .iter()
                    .any(|(name, _)| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(wanted))
            })
            .map(|face| {
                (
                    face.id,
                    face.index,
                    face.families.first().map(|(n, _)| n.clone()),
                )
            });
        let Some((id, index, name)) = family else {
            continue;
        };
        let data = db.with_face_data(id, |bytes, _| bytes.to_vec())?;
        if data.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        return Some(LoadedFont {
            family: name.unwrap_or_else(|| (*wanted).to_owned()),
            data,
            index,
        });
    }
    None
}

/// Extract the file name without its extension.
///
/// Both separators are handled explicitly rather than deferring to
/// `Path::file_stem`, so the Windows path list produces sensible names even
/// when this code is compiled and tested on Unix.
fn file_stem(path: &str) -> String {
    let name = path.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or(path);
    match name.rsplit_once('.') {
        Some((stem, _)) if !stem.is_empty() => stem.to_owned(),
        _ => name.to_owned(),
    }
}

/// The result of installing fonts into an egui context.
pub enum FontStatus {
    /// A CJK font was installed.
    Loaded(String),
    /// No CJK font was found; Chinese text will not render.
    Missing,
}

/// Family name of the font installed at startup.
///
/// Cached rather than re-discovered: the lookup reads a multi-megabyte font

static INSTALLED_FAMILY: std::sync::OnceLock<Option<String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();

/// Family name of the CJK font in use, or `None` when none was found.
pub fn installed_family() -> Option<String> {
    INSTALLED_FAMILY.get().cloned().flatten()
}

        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(ui_font.data);

        fonts.font_data.insert("zed_ui".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));
        fonts
            .families
            .entry(egui::FontFamily::Proportional)
            .or_default()
            .insert(0, "zed_ui".to_owned());
        let _ = INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.set(Some(ui_font.family));
    } else {
        let _ = INSTALLED_UI_FAMILY.set(None);
    }

    if let Some(mono_font) = find_mono_font() {
        let mut data = egui::FontData::from_owned(mono_font.data);
        data.index = mono_font.index;
        fonts.font_data.insert("zed_mono".to_owned(), Arc::new(data));
        fonts
            .families
            .entry(egui::FontFamily::Monospace)
            .or_default()

    let cjk = find_cjk_font();

        }
    }

        Some(font) => {
            let _ = INSTALLED_FAMILY.set(Some(font.family.clone()));
            FontStatus::Loaded(font.family)
        }
        None => {
            let _ = INSTALLED_FAMILY.set(None);
            FontStatus::Missing
//! Dark and light themes, and the colours used by the receive log.
//!
//! The original tool ships a black-background/green-text terminal look, plus a
//! "白底黑字" (white background, black text) alternative.  Both are preserved
//! here as the *log* palettes of the two themes, while the surrounding
//! application chrome follows a conventional dark/light widget theme.

use eframe::egui::{self, Color32, Stroke, Visuals};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Which theme the application should use.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ThemeMode {
    /// Classic terminal look: black log, green text.
    #[default]
    Dark,
    /// 白底黑字: white log, black text.
    Light,
    /// Follow the operating system preference.
    System,
}

impl ThemeMode {
    pub const ALL: [ThemeMode; 3] = [ThemeMode::Dark, ThemeMode::Light, ThemeMode::System];

    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ThemeMode::Dark => "黑色主题",
            ThemeMode::Light => "白色主题",
            ThemeMode::System => "跟随系统",
        }
    }

    pub fn icon(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ThemeMode::Dark => "🌙",
            ThemeMode::Light => "☀",
            ThemeMode::System => "🖥",
        }
    }
}

/// Colours for the receive log area.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LogPalette {
    pub background: Color32,
    pub foreground: Color32,
    /// Colour of the `[HH:MM:SS.mmm]` prefix.
    pub timestamp: Color32,
    /// Selection highlight.
    pub selection: Color32,
    /// Text of the selection.
    pub selection_text: Color32,
    /// Rows echoed back from our own transmissions.
    pub sent: Color32,
}

/// The classic XCOM terminal look.
pub const DARK_LOG: LogPalette = LogPalette {
    background: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0x00, 0x00),
    foreground: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0xFF, 0x00),
    timestamp: Color32::from_rgb(0x6A, 0xA8, 0x6A),
    selection: Color32::from_rgb(0x1E, 0x4D, 0x2E),
    selection_text: Color32::from_rgb(0xEA, 0xFF, 0xEA),
    // Amber reads clearly against the green of received data.
    sent: Color32::from_rgb(0xFF, 0xB7, 0x4D),
};

/// 白底黑字.
pub const LIGHT_LOG: LogPalette = LogPalette {
    background: Color32::from_rgb(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF),
    foreground: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0x00, 0x00),
    timestamp: Color32::from_rgb(0x80, 0x80, 0x80),
    selection: Color32::from_rgb(0xCC, 0xE4, 0xFF),
    selection_text: Color32::from_rgb(0x00, 0x00, 0x00),
    sent: Color32::from_rgb(0xB2, 0x5E, 0x00),
};

/// User override for the log colours.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct LogColorOverride {
    /// When false the theme's default log palette is used.
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub foreground: [u8; 3],
    pub background: [u8; 3],
}

impl Default for LogColorOverride {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            enabled: false,
            foreground: [0x00, 0xFF, 0x00],
            background: [0x00, 0x00, 0x00],
        }
    }
}

impl LogColorOverride {
    /// Apply the override on top of a theme palette.
    pub fn apply(self, base: LogPalette) -> LogPalette {
        if !self.enabled {
            return base;
        }
        let foreground =
            Color32::from_rgb(self.foreground[0], self.foreground[1], self.foreground[2]);
        let background =
            Color32::from_rgb(self.background[0], self.background[1], self.background[2]);
        // Keep the selection legible against whatever background was chosen.
        let selection = blend(background, foreground, 0.35);
        LogPalette {
            background,
            foreground,
            selection,
            selection_text: foreground,
            // Timestamps stay distinguishable without clashing.
            timestamp: blend(background, foreground, 0.65),
            // A custom foreground/background pair says nothing about which hue
            // suits echoed rows, so the theme's choice is kept.
            sent: base.sent,
        }
    }
}

/// Linear blend between two colours; `t` of 0 yields `a`, 1 yields `b`.
fn blend(a: Color32, b: Color32, t: f32) -> Color32 {
    let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
    let mix = |x: u8, y: u8| (x as f32 + (y as f32 - x as f32) * t).round() as u8;
    Color32::from_rgb(mix(a.r(), b.r()), mix(a.g(), b.g()), mix(a.b(), b.b()))
}

/// Background colour of the application chrome (panels and status bar).
///
/// Also used as the window backdrop, which is why it is public: the rounded
/// window background is painted in this colour.
pub fn panel_background(dark: bool) -> Color32 {
    if dark {
        Color32::from_rgb(0x1E, 0x1E, 0x1E)
    } else {
        Color32::from_rgb(0xF3, 0xF3, 0xF3)
    }
}

/// Whether the given mode currently resolves to a dark appearance.
pub fn is_dark(ctx: &egui::Context, mode: ThemeMode) -> bool {
    match mode {
        ThemeMode::Dark => true,
        ThemeMode::Light => false,
        ThemeMode::System => ctx.theme() == egui::Theme::Dark,
    }

        }
    }
}

impl XcomApp {
    /// Draw one complete frame.
    ///
    /// eframe 0.36 roots the app at a `Ui` rather than a `Context`, so the
    /// context is taken from it and used for the top-level panels.  Split out
    /// of the `App` impl so the headless test can lay out a real frame.
    pub(crate) fn draw(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) {
        let ctx = ui.ctx().clone();
        let ctx = &ctx;

        // The window backdrop goes down first, so every panel paints on top of
        // it.  Panels are transparent on platforms where we own the frame (see
        // `ui::window`), otherwise they would square off the bottom corners.
        crate::ui::window::paint_background(
            ui,
            crate::theme::panel_background(crate::theme::is_dark(ctx, self.settings.theme)),
        );

        // Styling only needs to be re-applied when the theme changes.
        let theme = self.settings.theme;
        if self.applied_theme != Some(theme) {
            crate::theme::apply(ctx, theme);
            self.applied_theme = Some(theme);
        }
        // The title bar is not re-read from the app, so switching language has
        // to push a new one; otherwise a Chinese UI keeps an English title
        // until the next launch.
        let language = crate::i18n::lang();
        if self.applied_lang != Some(language) {
            self.applied_lang = Some(language);
            ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Title(crate::i18n::window_title()));
        }

        // egui's default grab band is 5 px, which is easy to miss and presents
        // as "the separator cannot be dragged at all".
        ui.style_mut().interaction.resize_grab_radius_side = 8.0;

        self.note_font_status();

        self.pump_serial(ctx);
        self.pump_timers(ctx);
        self.handle_shortcuts(ctx);

        panels::top_bar(self, ui);
        panels::status_bar(self, ui);
        panels::left_panel(self, ui);
        if self.show_side_panel {
            panels::side_panel(self, ui);
        }

    let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
    let mix = |x: u8, y: u8| (x as f32 + (y as f32 - x as f32) * t).round() as u8;
    Color32::from_rgb(mix(a.r(), b.r()), mix(a.g(), b.g()), mix(a.b(), b.b()))
}

/// Background colour of the application chrome (panels and status bar).
///
/// Also used as the window backdrop, which is why it is public: the rounded
/// window background is painted in this colour.
pub fn panel_background(dark: bool) -> Color32 {
    if dark {
        Color32::from_rgb(0x1E, 0x1E, 0x1E)
    } else {
        Color32::from_rgb(0xF3, 0xF3, 0xF3)
    }
}

/// Whether the given mode currently resolves to a dark appearance.
pub fn is_dark(ctx: &egui::Context, mode: ThemeMode) -> bool {
    match mode {
        ThemeMode::Dark => true,
        ThemeMode::Light => false,
        ThemeMode::System => ctx.theme() == egui::Theme::Dark,
    }
}

/// The log palette in effect.
pub fn log_palette(ctx: &egui::Context, mode: ThemeMode, over: LogColorOverride) -> LogPalette {
    let base = if is_dark(ctx, mode) {
        DARK_LOG
    } else {
        LIGHT_LOG
    };
    over.apply(base)
}

/// Install the widget visuals for both themes and select the active one.
///
/// Called only when the mode changes, not every frame.
pub fn apply(ctx: &egui::Context, mode: ThemeMode) {
    ctx.set_visuals_of(egui::Theme::Dark, tuned_dark());
    ctx.set_visuals_of(egui::Theme::Light, tuned_light());
    ctx.set_theme(match mode {
        ThemeMode::Dark => egui::ThemePreference::Dark,
        ThemeMode::Light => egui::ThemePreference::Light,
        ThemeMode::System => egui::ThemePreference::System,
    });
    ctx.all_styles_mut(|style| {
        style.spacing.item_spacing = egui::vec2(8.0, 6.0);
        style.spacing.button_padding = egui::vec2(8.0, 4.0);
    });
}

- CRC16 is **CRC-16/MODBUS** (reflected polynomial `0xA001`, initial value `0xFFFF`), **low byte first**, consistent with Modbus RTU.
- Checksum (SUM) is the **two's complement** of the byte sum, i.e., the byte sum of the entire frame mod 256 equals 0.
- CRC8 is **CRC-8/MAXIM** (reflected polynomial `0x31`, initial value `0x00`); the checksum of `"123456789"` is `0xA1`.
- No start/stop delimiters: response frames are bounded by **bus idle time**, threshold = `320000 / baud_rate + 2` milliseconds.

Retransmission: the frame period is both the auto-send interval and the **retransmission timeout**. On timeout, it retransmits with the **same frame sequence**, up to `max retries` times, then reports "device no response". Only new logical frames increment the sequence (starting from 0, so the first frame's sequence is `1`).

Response validation: only the **frame sequence** and **checksum** (and length validity) are verified. Device address and function are marked as "arbitrary" per the official example — shown for display only, not validated.

> Frame format based on: the frame format diagram on the official v3.0 manual page, the same table in the official forum announcement, and decompiled `ManageTransportProtocol.cs` / `CheckTransportProtocol.cs` from the official XCOM binary (V2.3), cross-validated with real captured frames.
> The v3.0 page embeds the same frame format diagram and text and is verbatim identical to the 2013 announcement, so we infer v3.0 did not change this format (this is inference, not direct evidence).

### A Practical Constraint

The frame period **must be greater than the response frame-delimiting time**, otherwise retransmission fires before the response is recognized. The program warns when the frame period is too short.

## Desktop Integration (Linux)

`packaging/xcom.desktop` provides a desktop entry (Chinese and English names, categories, keywords). The `StartupWMClass=xcom` must match `ViewportBuilder::with_app_id("xcom")` in `src/main.rs`, otherwise the compositor can't associate the window with the entry, and the taskbar won't get the icon or correct name.

```bash
cargo build --release
sudo install -Dm755 target/release/xcom /usr/local/bin/xcom
sudo install -Dm644 packaging/xcom.desktop /usr/share/applications/xcom.desktop
sudo install -Dm644 packaging/xcom.png /usr/share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps/xcom.png
sudo update-desktop-database /usr/share/applications
sudo gtk-update-icon-cache -f /usr/share/icons/hicolor 2>/dev/null || true

重发机制：帧周期既是自动发送周期，也是**重发超时**。超时后以**相同帧序列**重发，
最多 `最大重发次数` 次，然后报「设备无响应」。只有新的逻辑帧才会递增帧序列
（从 0 开始，因此第一帧的帧序列为 `1`）。

响应校验：只校验**帧序列**与**校验值**（以及长度合法性）。设备地址与帧功能按官方示例
标注为「随意」，仅作显示，不参与校验。

> 帧格式依据：官方 v3.0 说明页的帧格式图、官方论坛公告中的同款表格，
> 以及从官方 XCOM 二进制（V2.3）反编译得到的 `ManageTransportProtocol.cs` /
> `CheckTransportProtocol.cs`，并用真实抓包帧交叉验证过。
> v3.0 页面嵌入了相同的帧格式图、文字说明与 2013 年公告逐字一致，
> 因此推断 v3.0 未改变该格式（这一步是推断而非直接证据）。

### 一个实用的约束

帧周期**必须大于响应断帧时间**，否则会在响应被识别之前就重发。程序会在帧周期过小时给出提示。
```

pub struct Galley {
    /// The job that this galley is the result of.
    /// Contains the original string and style sections.
    pub job: Arc<LayoutJob>,

    /// Rows of text, from top to bottom, and their offsets.
    ///
    /// The number of characters in all rows sum up to `job.text.chars().count()`
    /// unless [`Self::elided`] is `true`.
    ///
    /// Note that a paragraph (a piece of text separated with `\n`)
    /// can be split up into multiple rows.
    pub rows: Vec<PlacedRow>,

    /// Set to true the text was truncated due to [`TextWrapping::max_rows`].
    pub elided: bool,

    /// Bounding rect.
    ///
    /// `rect.top()` is always 0.0.
    ///
    /// With [`LayoutJob::halign`]:
    /// * [`Align::LEFT`]: `rect.left() == 0.0`
    /// * [`Align::Center`]: `rect.center() == 0.0`
    /// * [`Align::RIGHT`]: `rect.right() == 0.0`
    pub rect: Rect,

    /// Tight bounding box around all the meshes in all the rows.
    /// Can be used for culling.
    pub mesh_bounds: Rect,

    /// Total number of vertices in all the row meshes.
    pub num_vertices: usize,

    /// Total number of indices in all the row meshes.
    pub num_indices: usize,

    /// The number of physical pixels for each logical point.
    /// Since this affects the layout, we keep track of it
    /// so that we can warn if this has changed once we get to
    /// tessellation.
    pub pixels_per_point: f32,

    pub(crate) intrinsic_size: Vec2,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize))]
pub struct PlacedRow {
    /// The position of this [`Row`] relative to the galley.
    ///
    /// This is rounded to the closest _pixel_ in order to produce crisp, pixel-perfect text.
    pub pos: Pos2,

    /// The underlying unpositioned [`Row`].
    pub row: Arc<Row>,

    /// If true, this [`PlacedRow`] came from a paragraph ending with a `\n`.
    /// The `\n` itself is omitted from row's [`Row::glyphs`].
    /// A `\n` in the input text always creates a new [`PlacedRow`] below it,
    /// so that text that ends with `\n` has an empty [`PlacedRow`] last.
    /// This also implies that the last [`PlacedRow`] in a [`Galley`] always has `ends_with_newline == false`.
    pub ends_with_newline: bool,
}

impl PlacedRow {
    /// Logical bounding rectangle on font heights etc.
    ///
    /// This ignores / includes the `LayoutSection::leading_space`.
    pub fn rect(&self) -> Rect {
        Rect::from_min_size(self.pos, self.row.size)
    }

    /// Same as [`Self::rect`] but excluding the `LayoutSection::leading_space`.
    pub fn rect_without_leading_space(&self) -> Rect {
        let x = self.pos.x + self.glyphs.first().map_or(0.0, |g| g.pos.x);
        let right = self.pos.x + self.size.x;
        Rect::from_min_max(
            Pos2::new(x, self.pos.y),
            Pos2::new(right, self.pos.y + self.size.y),
        )
    }
}

impl core::ops::Deref for PlacedRow {
    type Target = Row;

    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
        &self.row
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize))]
pub struct Row {
    /// This is included in case there are no glyphs.

/// The tessellated output of a row.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize))]
pub struct RowVisuals {
    /// The tessellated text, using non-normalized (texel) UV coordinates.
    /// That is, you need to divide the uv coordinates by the texture size.

    ///

impl Default for RowVisuals {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            mesh: Default::default(),

/// Describes the task of laying out text.
///
/// This supports mixing different fonts, color and formats (underline etc).
///
/// Pass this to [`crate::FontsView::layout_job`] or [`crate::text::layout`].
///
/// ## Example:
/// ```
/// use epaint::{Color32, text::{LayoutJob, TextFormat}, FontFamily, FontId};
///
/// let mut job = LayoutJob::default();
/// job.append(
///     "Hello ",
///     0.0,
///     TextFormat {
///         font_id: FontId::new(14.0, FontFamily::Proportional),
///         color: Color32::WHITE,
///         ..Default::default()
///     },
/// );
/// job.append(
///     "World!",
///     0.0,
///     TextFormat {
///         font_id: FontId::new(14.0, FontFamily::Monospace),
///         color: Color32::BLACK,
///         ..Default::default()
///     },
/// );
/// ```
///
/// As you can see, constructing a [`LayoutJob`] is currently a lot of work.
/// It would be nice to have a helper macro for it!
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize))]
pub struct LayoutJob {
    /// The complete text of this job, referenced by [`LayoutSection`].
    pub text: String,

    /// The different section, which can have different fonts, colors, etc.
    ///
    /// Invariant: the sections are ordered by their `byte_range`,
    /// and together cover the whole of [`Self::text`] with no gaps and no overlaps.
    /// That is: the first section starts at byte 0, the last section ends at `text.len()`,
    /// and each section starts exactly where the previous one ended.
    /// This is checked by [`Self::debug_sanity_check`].
    pub sections: Vec<LayoutSection>,

    /// Controls the text wrapping and elision.
    pub wrap: TextWrapping,

    /// The first row must be at least this high.
    /// This is in case we lay out text that is the continuation
    /// of some earlier text (sharing the same row),
    /// in which case this will be the height of the earlier text.
    /// In other cases, set this to `0.0`.
    pub first_row_min_height: f32,

    /// If `true`, all `\n` characters will result in a new _paragraph_,
    /// starting on a new row.
    ///
    /// If `false`, all `\n` characters will be ignored
    /// and show up as the replacement character.
    ///
    /// Default: `true`.
    pub break_on_newline: bool,

impl Row {
    /// The text on this row, excluding the implicit `\n` if any.
    pub fn text(&self) -> String {
        self.glyphs.iter().map(|g| g.chr).collect()
    }

    /// Excludes the implicit `\n` after the [`Row`], if any.
    #[inline]
    pub fn char_count_excluding_newline(&self) -> CharIndex {
        CharIndex(self.glyphs.len())
    }

    /// Closest char at the desired x coordinate in row-relative coordinates.
    /// Returns something in the range `[0, char_count_excluding_newline()]`.
    pub fn char_at(&self, desired_x: f32) -> CharIndex {
        for (i, glyph) in self.glyphs.iter().enumerate() {
            if desired_x < glyph.logical_rect().center().x {
                return CharIndex(i);
            }
        }
        self.char_count_excluding_newline()
    }

    pub fn x_offset(&self, column: CharIndex) -> f32 {
        if let Some(glyph) = self.glyphs.get(column.0) {
            glyph.pos.x
        } else {
            self.size.x
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn height(&self) -> f32 {
        self.size.y
    }
}

impl PlacedRow {
    #[inline]
    pub fn min_y(&self) -> f32 {
        self.rect().top()
    }

    #[inline]
    pub fn max_y(&self) -> f32 {
        self.rect().bottom()
    }

    /// Includes the implicit `\n` after the [`PlacedRow`], if any.
    #[inline]
    pub fn char_count_including_newline(&self) -> CharIndex {
        CharIndex(self.row.glyphs.len() + (self.ends_with_newline as usize))
    }
}

/// Calculate the Y positions and tessellate the text.
fn galley_from_rows(
    point_scale: PointScale,
    job: Arc<LayoutJob>,
    mut rows: Vec<PlacedRow>,
    elided: bool,
    intrinsic_size: Vec2,
) -> Galley {
    let mut first_row_min_height = job.first_row_min_height;
    let mut cursor_y = 0.0;

    for placed_row in &mut rows {
        let mut max_row_height = first_row_min_height.at_least(placed_row.height());
        let row = Arc::make_mut(&mut placed_row.row);

        first_row_min_height = 0.0;
        for glyph in &row.glyphs {
            max_row_height = max_row_height.at_least(glyph.line_height);
        }
        max_row_height = point_scale.round_to_pixel(max_row_height);

        // Now position each glyph vertically:
        for glyph in &mut row.glyphs {
            let format = &job.sections[glyph.section_index as usize].format;

            glyph.pos.y = glyph.font_face_ascent

                // Apply valign to the different in height of the entire row, and the height of this `Font`:
                + format.valign.to_factor() * (max_row_height - glyph.line_height)

                // When mixing different `FontImpl` (e.g. latin and emojis),
                // we always center the difference:
                + 0.5 * (glyph.font_height - glyph.font_face_height);

            glyph.pos.y = point_scale.round_to_pixel(glyph.pos.y);
        }

        placed_row.pos.y = cursor_y;
        row.size.y = max_row_height;

        cursor_y += max_row_height;
        cursor_y = point_scale.round_to_pixel(cursor_y); // TODO(emilk): it would be better to do the calculations in pixels instead.
    }

///

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Eq, Hash, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize))]
pub enum FontFamily {
    /// A font where some characters are wider than other (e.g. 'w' is wider than 'i').
    ///
    /// Proportional fonts are easier to read and should be the preferred choice in most situations.
    #[default]
    Proportional,

    /// A font where each character is the same width (`w` is the same width as `i`).
    ///
    /// Useful for code snippets, or when you need to align numbers or text.
    Monospace,

    /// One of the names in [`FontDefinitions::families`].
    ///
    /// ```
    /// # use epaint::FontFamily;
    /// // User-chosen names:
    /// FontFamily::Name("arial".into());
    /// FontFamily::Name("serif".into());
    /// ```
    Name(Arc<str>),
}

impl core::fmt::Display for FontFamily {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::Monospace => "Monospace".fmt(f),
            Self::Proportional => "Proportional".fmt(f),
            Self::Name(name) => (*name).fmt(f),
        }
    }
}

    /// Show the combo box, with the given ui code for the menu contents.
    ///
    /// Returns `InnerResponse { inner: None }` if the combo box is closed.
    pub fn show_ui<R>(
        self,
        ui: &mut Ui,
        menu_contents: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui) -> R,
    ) -> InnerResponse<Option<R>> {
        self.show_ui_dyn(ui, Box::new(menu_contents))
    }

    fn show_ui_dyn<'c, R>(
        self,
        ui: &mut Ui,
        menu_contents: Box<dyn FnOnce(&mut Ui) -> R + 'c>,
    ) -> InnerResponse<Option<R>> {
        let Self {
            id_salt,
            label,
            selected_text,
            width,
            height,
            icon,
            wrap_mode,
            close_behavior,
            popup_style,
        } = self;

        let button_id = ui.make_persistent_id(id_salt);

        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            let mut ir = combo_box_dyn(
                ui,
                button_id,
                selected_text.clone(),
                menu_contents,
                icon,
                wrap_mode,
                close_behavior,
                popup_style,
                (width, height),
            );
            ir.response.widget_info(|| {
                let mut info = WidgetInfo::new(WidgetType::ComboBox);
                info.enabled = ui.is_enabled();
                info.current_text_value = Some(selected_text.text().to_owned());
                info
            });
            if let Some(label) = label {
                let label_response = ui.label(label);
                ir.response = ir.response.labelled_by(label_response.id);
                ir.response |= label_response;
            }
            ir
        })
        .inner
    }

//! Every visible panel of the application.
//!
//! The layout mirrors the original tool: configuration down the left, the
//! receive log filling the middle, the send area beneath it, and the
//! multi-send / protocol-transfer pages in a panel on the right.  A status bar
//! along the bottom carries the byte counters, the handshake lines and the
//! clock.

use eframe::egui::{self, Context, RichText, Ui};
use std::path::PathBuf;

use crate::app::{draw_log, Level, SideTab, XcomApp};
use crate::encoding::EncodingId;
use crate::i18n::{self, tr, Lang};
use crate::logstore::{HexStyle, ViewMode};
use crate::protocol::{ChecksumKind, TaskKind};
use crate::serial::config::{CUSTOM_BAUD_RANGE, STANDARD_BAUDS};
use crate::serial::{DataBitsSel, FlowSel, ParitySel, StopBitsSel};
use crate::theme::{self, ThemeMode};

/// Where a test can read what the real panels actually laid out.
///
/// The drag tests must measure the production code path rather than a
/// stand-in, or they pass whether or not the fix is present.  Outside tests
/// every setter is an empty function that inlines away.
pub(crate) mod probe {
    #[cfg(test)]
    use eframe::egui;
    #[cfg(test)]

        static SEND_PANEL_RECT: Cell<egui::Rect> = const { Cell::new(egui::Rect::NOTHING) };
        static EDITOR_RECT: Cell<egui::Rect> = const { Cell::new(egui::Rect::NOTHING) };
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn set_left_content_width(width: f32) {

    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub(crate) fn set_left_content_width(_width: f32) {}

        LEFT_CONTENT_WIDTH.with(|c| c.get())
    }

    }

/// Serial-settings panel width, in points.
pub(crate) const LEFT_PANEL_DEFAULT: f32 = 272.0;
pub(crate) const LEFT_PANEL_MIN: f32 = 232.0;
pub(crate) const LEFT_PANEL_MAX: f32 = 460.0;

/// Tool panel width.  The default is two thirds of the original 430 so the
/// receive area gets more room out of the box.
pub(crate) const RIGHT_PANEL_DEFAULT: f32 = 287.0;
pub(crate) const RIGHT_PANEL_MIN: f32 = 260.0;
pub(crate) const RIGHT_PANEL_MAX: f32 = 760.0;

/// Height of the send area.

    #[test]
    fn shrinking_the_settings_panel_persists() {
        // Reported: dragging the left separator *left* clipped the panel's
        // content during the gesture and then snapped back on release, while
        // the receive area never grew.
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let mut app = XcomApp::headless(crate::settings::Settings::default());
        app.show_side_panel = false;

        let before = full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input());
        let grab = egui::pos2(before.min.x, before.center().y);
        drag(&ctx, &mut app, grab, egui::pos2(grab.x - 40.0, grab.y));

        let after = full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input());
        assert!(
            after.min.x < before.min.x - 20.0,
            "the panel snapped back instead of staying shrunk: {} -> {}",
            before.min.x,
            after.min.x
        );

        // And it must still be shrunk several frames later, i.e. the size was
        // committed rather than merely applied for one frame.
        for _ in 0..5 {
            full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input());
        }
        assert!(
            full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input()).min.x < before.min.x - 20.0,
            "the shrunk size was not persisted"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn tool_panel_splitter_boundary_consistent_in_all_languages() {
        let _guard = crate::i18n::test_lock();
        let mut right_edges = Vec::new();
        for language in [crate::i18n::Lang::ZhCn, crate::i18n::Lang::EnUs] {
            crate::i18n::set_lang(language);
            let ctx = egui::Context::default();
            let mut app = XcomApp::headless(crate::settings::Settings::default());
            app.side_tab = SideTab::Multi;
            let center = full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input());
            right_edges.push((language, center.max.x));
        }
        crate::i18n::set_lang(crate::i18n::Lang::ZhCn);
        let zh_edge = right_edges[0].1;
        let en_edge = right_edges[1].1;
        assert_eq!(
            zh_edge, en_edge,
            "Splitter boundary must be identical across languages: ZhCn={zh_edge}, EnUs={en_edge}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn shrinking_the_tool_panel_persists_in_every_language() {
        // Reported: in English the tool panel snapped back when shrunk; in
        // Chinese it did not, which points at something width-dependent in the
        // translated strings.
        //
        // We drag by 25 px — small enough to stay above RIGHT_PANEL_MIN
        // (DEFAULT 287 − 25 = 262 > MIN 260) so the panel actually moves
        // and the result is not clamped away.  The key assertion is that
        // the moved position is *retained* across several frames, i.e. the
        // panel did not snap back.
        let _guard = crate::i18n::test_lock();
        for language in [crate::i18n::Lang::ZhCn, crate::i18n::Lang::EnUs] {
            crate::i18n::set_lang(language);
            let ctx = egui::Context::default();
            let mut app = XcomApp::headless(crate::settings::Settings::default());
            app.side_tab = SideTab::Multi;

            let before = full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input());
            // The right panel's left edge; shrinking it moves this right.
            let grab = egui::pos2(before.max.x, before.center().y);
            drag(&ctx, &mut app, grab, egui::pos2(grab.x + 25.0, grab.y));
        if let Err(e) = app.link.open(&app.settings.serial) {
            eprintln!("skipping: cannot open serial port: {e}");
            return;
        }

        app.settings.send.buffer = "AT".to_owned();
        app.settings.send.append_newline = false;
        app.settings.send.timed = true;
        app.settings.send.period_ms = 30;

        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(250);
        while Instant::now() < deadline {
            let mut output = ctx.run_ui(input(), |ui| app.draw(ui));
            output.textures_delta.clear();
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5));
        }

        let got = pty.read_available(Duration::from_millis(100));
        println!(
            "link_open={} messages={:?}",
            app.link.is_open(),
            app.messages.iter().map(|m| &m.text).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&got);
        assert!(
            text.matches("AT").count() >= 2,
            "expected the payload repeatedly, got {text:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn settings_that_need_a_control_have_one_in_the_ui() {
        // The echo feature shipped with the setting wired through the store and
        // the send path but *no* control anywhere, so the user could neither
        // see nor change it.  Every behavioural test passed because they set
        // the field directly.  This checks the other half: that the panels
        // actually offer a control for each setting a user is meant to reach.
        let panels =
            std::fs::read_to_string(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/ui/panels.rs"))
                .expect("panels.rs is readable");
        for field in [
            "echo_sent",
            "auto_scroll",
            "log_font_size",
            "line_spacing",
            "loop_enabled",
            "loop_count",
        ] {
            // The write, not merely a mention: reading a field proves nothing
            // about whether a control can change it.
            assert!(
                panels.contains(&format!("{field} = ")),
                "settings.{field} has no control that sets it"
            );
        }
    }

        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let mut app = XcomApp::headless(crate::settings::Settings::default());
        render(&mut app, &ctx, "empty log");

    fn renders_the_interface_in_english() {
        // The guard test proves every key has a translation; this proves the
        // whole frame actually lays out in English without panicking.
        let _guard = crate::i18n::test_lock();
        crate::i18n::set_lang(crate::i18n::Lang::EnUs);
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let mut app = seeded();
        app.show_about = true;
        for tab in [SideTab::Multi, SideTab::Protocol] {
            app.side_tab = tab;
            render(&mut app, &ctx, "english");

        crate::i18n::set_lang(crate::i18n::Lang::ZhCn);
        render(&mut app, &ctx, "chinese");
    }

fn display_section(app: &mut XcomApp, ui: &mut Ui) {
    egui::CollapsingHeader::new(tr("显示设置"))
        .default_open(true)
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            let mut display = app.settings.display;
            let mut changed = false;

            let mut hex = display.mode == ViewMode::Hex;
            if ui.checkbox(&mut hex, tr("16进制显示")).changed() {
                display.mode = if hex { ViewMode::Hex } else { ViewMode::Text };
                changed = true;
            }

            if display.mode == ViewMode::Hex {
                ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                    ui.label(tr("HEX 样式"));
                    let mut style = display.hex_style;
                    if combo(
                        ui,
                        "hex_style",
                        &mut style,
                        &[HexStyle::Stream, HexStyle::Dump],
                        |s| match s {
                            HexStyle::Stream => tr("连续").to_owned(),
                            HexStyle::Dump => tr("16 字节/行").to_owned(),
                        },
                    ) {
                        display.hex_style = style;
                        changed = true;
                    }
                    let mut upper = display.upper_hex;
                    if ui.checkbox(&mut upper, tr("大写")).changed() {
                        display.upper_hex = upper;
                        changed = true;
                    }
                });
                if display.hex_style == HexStyle::Dump {
                    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                        ui.label(tr("每行字节"));
                        let mut per_row = display.hex_bytes_per_row;
                        if ui
                            .add(egui::DragValue::new(&mut per_row).range(1..=64))
                            .changed()
        Some(text) => {
            ui.ctx().copy_text(text);
            app.ok(tr("已复制选中内容到剪贴板"));
        }
        None => app.warn(tr("没有可复制的内容")),
    }
}

/// Lay out only the send editor and report the height it took, so a test can
/// observe that dragging the separator really resizes it.
fn send_area(app: &mut XcomApp, ui: &mut Ui) {
    probe::set_send_panel_rect(ui.max_rect());
    probe::begin_send_toolbar();

    // Toolbar row height: tall enough that text/checkboxes are not clipped.
    const BTN_HEIGHT: f32 = 28.0;
    // Right margin between the 发送 button and the panel edge.
    const RIGHT_PAD: f32 = 6.0;

    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
        ui.set_height(BTN_HEIGHT);
        ui.spacing_mut().item_spacing = egui::vec2(6.0, 0.0);

        // ── Left: label + configuration controls ────────────────────────────
        ui.label(RichText::new(tr("发送区")).strong());
        ui.separator();

        let mut hex = app.settings.send.hex;
        if ui.checkbox(&mut hex, tr("16进制发送")).changed() {
            app.settings.send.hex = hex;
            app.mark_settings_dirty();
        }
        let mut newline = app.settings.send.append_newline;
        if ui.checkbox(&mut newline, tr("发送新行")).changed() {
            app.settings.send.append_newline = newline;
            app.mark_settings_dirty();
        }
        if app.settings.send.append_newline {
            let mut cr = app.settings.send.newline_cr;
            let mut lf = app.settings.send.newline_lf;
            let a = ui.checkbox(&mut cr, "CR").changed();
            let b = ui.checkbox(&mut lf, "LF").changed();
            if a || b {
                app.settings.send.newline_cr = cr;
                app.settings.send.newline_lf = lf;
                app.mark_settings_dirty();
            }
        }

        let mut timed = app.settings.send.timed;
        let can_timed = app.link.is_open();
        if ui
            .add_enabled(can_timed, egui::Checkbox::new(&mut timed, tr("定时发送")))
            .changed()
        {
            app.settings.send.timed = timed;
            app.mark_settings_dirty();
        }
        if app.settings.send.timed {
            let mut period = app.settings.send.period_ms;
            if ui
                .add(
                    egui::DragValue::new(&mut period)
                        .speed(10.0)
                        .range(1..=3_600_000)
                        .suffix(" ms"),
                )
                .changed()
            {
                app.settings.send.period_ms = period;
                app.mark_settings_dirty();

    // egui's `Grid` reuses the previous frame's column widths as a *floor*
    // (`child_size.max(prev_width)`), so a table built with it can grow but
    // never shrink -- dragging the splitter back left the columns too wide and
    // pushed the send button off the edge.  Laying the rows out by hand with
    // explicit widths is what makes them track the panel in both directions.
    //
    // These five widths must sum to the `fixed` constant in
    // `multi_column_widths`, or the row will not fill the panel exactly.
    let enable_w = 30.0;
    let index_w = 24.0;
    let hex_w = 30.0;
    let newline_w = 32.0;
    // Delay applied after this entry, before the next one.
    let delay_w = 58.0;
    let send_w = 52.0;

    const ROW_H: f32 = 20.0;
    const GAP: f32 = 5.0;

    let (text_width, note_width) = multi_column_widths(ui.available_width(), GAP);

    // Fill the panel with rows rather than fixing each page at ten entries.
    let rows_that_fit = ((ui.available_height() - ROW_H * 1.5) / (ROW_H + 4.0)).floor();
    let visible = rows_that_fit.max(crate::multi::ENTRIES_PER_PAGE as f32) as usize;
    if app.settings.multi.ensure_len(page, visible) {
        app.mark_settings_dirty();
        dirty = true;
    }
    let total_rows = app
        .settings
        .multi
        .pages
        .get(page)
        .map_or(0, Vec::len)
        .max(visible);

    egui::ScrollArea::both()
        .auto_shrink([false, false])
        .show(ui, |ui| {
            ui.spacing_mut().item_spacing = egui::vec2(GAP, 4.0);

    #[test]
    fn open_port_button_is_horizontally_centered() {
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let mut app = seeded();

        full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input());

        let content = panels::probe::serial_content_rect();
        let button = panels::probe::open_button_rect();
        assert!(content.width() > 0.0, "serial content was not laid out");
        assert!(button.width() > 0.0, "open button was not laid out");
        let offset = (button.center().x - content.center().x).abs();
        assert!(

        );

    fn send_history_combobox_matches_action_button_height() {
        let ctx = egui::Context::default();
        let mut app = seeded();

        full_frame(&ctx, &mut app, input());

        let rects = panels::probe::send_toolbar_rects();
        let find = |name: &str| {
            rects
                .iter()
                .find(|(candidate, _)| *candidate == name)
                .map(|(_, rect)| *rect)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{name} control was not laid out"))
        };
        let history = find("history");
        let send = find("send");
        let file = find("file");
        let clear = find("clear");
        for (name, rect) in [("file", file), ("clear", clear)] {
            assert!(
                (rect.height() - send.height()).abs() <= 0.25,
                "{name} height {:.2} differs from send {:.2}",
                rect.height(),
                send.height()
            );
        }
        assert!(
            (history.height() - send.height()).abs() <= 0.25,
            "history height {:.2} differs from send button {:.2}",
            history.height(),
            send.height()
        );
        assert!(
            (history.center().y - send.center().y).abs() <= 0.5,
            "history is vertically misaligned by {:.2}px",
            (history.center().y - send.center().y).abs()
        );
